items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: How to Sue an Energy Project After the Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports that the bill's judicial-review remedy provision could make most of its NEPA sections matter less, per a former DOJ environment official.

quote.text: remaining 100 pages of the bill devoted to NEPA are all going to be irrelevant in light of that remedy provision
quote.speaker: Matthew Littleton

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Jared Huffman Wants to See Some Changes to the Senate’s Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports on Rep. Jared Huffman's written criticism of the bill's judgment-fund provision, which he says pays developers without approving projects.

quote.text: might pay some clean energy developers money from the judgment fund when they are screwed, but nothing to actually approve their projects
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Is Trump Trying to Blow Up the Permitting Deal?
items.summary: Heatmap reports the administration asked a court to re-examine a Revolution Wind permit, and argues the biggest risk to the deal is inside the administration.

quote.text: the biggest threat to the bipartisan permitting deal probably isn’t green groups, the fossil fuel industry, or monopoly utilities
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Permitting Reform’s Battle Lines Are Taking Shape
items.summary: Heatmap Daily reports that many environmental and climate nonprofits are split on the bill a week after its release.

quote.text: It’s now been just over a week since a gang of four bipartisan senators released the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: The Crucial Hardhat Union That Has Yet to Endorse the Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports on building-trades unions' positions on the bill, noting that much of the hardhat sector is now signing on as supporters.

quote.text: Now, with a permitting bill negotiated by two Democrats and two Republicans in the Senate, much of the hardhat union sector is signing on as eager supporters
quote.speaker: Matthew Zeitlin

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: Miners Struck Gold With the Senate Permitting Bill
items.summary: Heatmap reports that the bill's mining-waste provision would resolve a 2022 court problem for hardrock mining projects such as Rosemont.

quote.text: The proposal resolves an issue that has bedeviled the industry since 2022.
quote.speaker: Matthew Zeitlin

items.title: Senate permitting reform bill raises concerns for Tribal Nations' participation
items.summary: New Mexico Sun reports the Native American Rights Fund's Oct. 15 statement that the bill could weaken Tribal Nations' participation in federal project approvals.

quote.text: could significantly impact Tribal Nations' ability to participate in federal project approvals, according to an Oct. 15 statement from the Native American Rights Fund
quote.speaker: New Mexico Sun

items.author: Legis1 Editorial
items.title: Federal Energy Bill Could Override Objections by States
items.summary: Legis1 explains that the bill's FERC siting backstop could override state objections to transmission lines, a dispute with a long court and congressional history.

quote.text: The bill's title signals bipartisan support, which is notable given that transmission siting has historically divided lawmakers along regional and jurisdictional lines.
quote.speaker: Legis1 Editorial

items.author: Katie Brigham
items.title: An Unexpected Beneficiary of the Permitting Bill: Mini Marine Power
items.summary: Heatmap analyzes the bill's marine and hydrokinetic licensing provisions, which it presents as a major win for small wave, tidal and river-current projects.

quote.text: Tucked inside the Senate’s ambitious new permitting bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, is a major win for an energy technology that often flies under the radar: marine power.
quote.speaker: Katie Brigham

items.author: Peter Ross, Kevin Y. Chen
items.title: BAAJA Blast: What the Senate Permitting Bill Means for Transmission Developers
items.summary: Foley Hoag reviews the bill's transmission-siting and FERC provisions for developers and notes it must still pass both chambers and be signed.

quote.text: It must pass both chambers and be signed by the President, and it is not expected to be taken up until after the midterm elections
quote.speaker: Foley Hoag

items.author: Kainoa Lowman
items.title: The Senate’s Surprisingly Populist Permitting Reform Deal
items.summary: Washington Monthly argues the bill could lower electricity costs by targeting utilities, and describes its populist framing.

quote.text: could lower electricity costs and speed the green energy transition by targeting utilities
quote.speaker: Kainoa Lowman

items.author: Greenberg Traurig LLP
items.title: Senate Negotiators Reach Agreement on Permitting Reform Text
items.summary: Greenberg Traurig summarizes the Sept. 30 Senate negotiators' text and its mandatory agency deadlines and streamlined permitting for energy, transmission, pipeline and mining projects.

quote.text: The bill seeks to accelerate energy infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, pipeline, and mining project approvals through mandatory agency deadlines and streamlined permitting
quote.speaker: Greenberg Traurig

items.author: Ryan M. Bernstein, Bernard L. McNamee
items.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 Proposes Sweeping Reform for Energy and Infrastructure Projects
items.summary: McGuireWoods alert on the Sept. 30 committee agreement, covering permitting and environmental review changes plus transmission and large-load provisions, and noting the bill still needs both chambers.

quote.text: Senate committee leaders reached a bipartisan agreement on Sept. 30, 2026, on sweeping permitting reform for energy and infrastructure projects, but the bill still needs Senate and House approval
quote.speaker: McGuireWoods

items.author: W. Andrew Jack, Jayni Hein, Gary S. Guzy, Nicholas Xenakis
items.title: Senate Unveils Bipartisan Permitting Bill: What the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act Would Mean for Energy and Environmental Permitting
items.summary: Covington's energy practice summarizes the bill's key provisions by impact area, saying it would codify some existing NEPA reforms and go further in others.

quote.text: To some extent BAAJA would codify environmental review reforms which have been developed under several Administrations; in other respects, the proposed changes would be novel and potentially far-reaching.
quote.speaker: Covington authors

items.title: Senate Bipartisan Permitting Reform Package: What Economic Developers Need to Know
items.summary: The International Economic Development Council explains the 417-page bill for economic developers, describing it as the product of months of bipartisan negotiations.

quote.text: The 417-page bill is the result of months of bipartisan negotiations and would make changes to federal permitting and environmental review processes for energy, infrastructure, and other major projects.
quote.speaker: IEDC

items.author: Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP
items.title: Senate Unveils Bipartisan Comprehensive Permitting Reform Bill
items.summary: Akin's alert, republished on Mondaq, describes the bill as addressing longstanding concerns about complex, unpredictable and litigation-prone federal permitting.

quote.text: The bill seeks to address longstanding concerns that federal permitting and environmental review processes have become increasingly complex, unpredictable, and vulnerable to litigation.
quote.speaker: Akin Gump

items.author: Beveridge & Diamond PC
items.title: Senate Permitting Bill Would Reshape Environmental Permitting And Reviews
items.summary: Beveridge & Diamond, republished on Mondaq, says the bill would change environmental rules for energy and mineral projects by targeting certainty, streamlining and litigation.

quote.text: The bill would dramatically change environmental rules governing project development, especially for energy and mineral projects, by increasing permitting certainty, streamlining permitting processes, limiting litigation
quote.speaker: Beveridge & Diamond

items.author: Steve Hanley
items.title: US Senate Proposes New Permitting Framework. Should It Become Law?
items.summary: CleanTechnica explains the bill's proposed permitting framework and stresses that it is not yet law.

quote.text: Make no mistake, the bill Senator Whitehouse has helped craft is not a law yet.
quote.speaker: Steve Hanley

items.author: Native American Rights Fund
items.title: ACT NOW: Senate Permitting Reform Bill Negatively Impacts Tribes
items.summary: The Native American Rights Fund says the bill's shorter review timelines and narrower review triggers reduce federal oversight and tribal participation, and urges opposition.

quote.text: By imposing shorter review timelines and narrower definitions of what triggers a review, BAAJA reduces critical federal oversight and participation.
quote.speaker: Native American Rights Fund

items.author: Congressional Research Service
items.title: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's Backstop Siting Authority
items.summary: CRS Insight IN12746 explains how the bill would change FERC's authority to issue construction permits for transmission projects when states deny them.

quote.text: The bill would address numerous aspects of energy infrastructure permitting, including by amending the conditions under which the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) may issue a construction permit
quote.speaker: Congressional Research Service

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Should Climate Activists Keep Fighting Fossil Fuel Infrastructure?
items.summary: Shift Key episode 156, with SEI researcher Peter Erickson, opens by placing the bipartisan permitting bill in the Senate and asks whether climate activists should keep fighting fossil infrastructure.

quote.text: Hello, it's October 16, and the Senate is considering a bipartisan permitting bill.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer

items.author: David Roberts
items.title: What’s up with the new federal permitting reform bill?
items.summary: David Roberts interviews Daniel Palken of Arnold Ventures about the bill's transmission, data-center cost, NEPA and permit-certainty provisions.

quote.text: It brings us to kind of what is the energy sector for? What are we trying to do in this country?
quote.speaker: Daniel Palken

items.author: Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: Data center owners should pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades
items.summary: Sen. Martin Heinrich says the bill makes it mandatory for data center owners to pay for their electricity and grid upgrades.

quote.text: Data center owners should pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades–not you. Our new permitting reform bill makes that mandatory.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

items.author: Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: If we want cheaper energy, we need permitting reform.
items.summary: Sen. Martin Heinrich links cheaper energy to permitting reform and says the reform is in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act.

quote.text: And all of that reform is in our Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

events.title: Trump administration asks court to re-examine Revolution Wind permit
events.summary: The Trump administration asked a court to re-examine a key permit for the Revolution Wind offshore project in Rhode Island. Heatmap reports the move as a risk to the bipartisan permitting deal.
events.significance: Offshore-wind permit fights are the kind of executive action the bill's permit-certainty provisions are meant to foreclose.
